text:
nina: Hey team — filing a quick one. I'm requesting a financial hardship distribution from the 401(k) due to sudden medical bills. Plan portal says documentation required; vendor migration is next week (2026-09-14 -> 2026-09-18). Will migration slow verification? Any special notarization or ID requirements I should plan for?

ola: Sorry to hear that, @nina. Short answer: PlanHive processes hardship packets manually and may need PDFs of invoices/medical bills. Migrations sometimes slow portal uploads; best to email PlanHive docs directly and cc benefits@redwood.

payroll: Migration note: payroll vendor cutover is 2026-09-14 -> 09-18. That affects automated feeds but PlanHive's admin team still accepts email and manual processing. If you submit docs before 2026-09-13 EOD, it's less likely to hit cutover delays.

planbot: PlanHive policy excerpt: "Hardship distributions require supporting documentation (medical bills, proof of payment, or provider statement). Certain high-value distributions may require identity verification (government ID) and a signed hardship attestation. Notarization is not routinely required but may be requested in exceptional cases. Processing times may be extended during vendor system maintenance windows."

nina: Thanks. I have a $6,200 balance and a small outstanding loan @ $400. Can I get the hardship distribution that includes a loan offset? Will the loan portion be treated differently?

trevor: Plan mechanics: if you request a hardship distribution, the plan may net any outstanding loan balance from the distribution proceeds (i.e., distribution = vested balance - loan). If loan > distribution, you'll have a remaining balance treated per loan policy. Also, if loan offset occurs, the offset amount is treated as a taxable distribution and reported on 1099-R.

ola: Actionable steps for you @nina: 1) Start hardship case in PlanHive portal and upload medical docs. 2) Email docs to support@planhive.com and cc benefits@redwood. 3) If you prefer faster handling, attach a short cover email listing: LoanID, desired distribution amount, whether to net loan. Example cover text: 
```
Employee: nina
LoanID: 990123
Requested hardship amount: $6,200
Net loan from distribution: yes
Contact phone: (xxx) xxx-xxxx
```
4) If you want loan to be repaid instead of netting, you can ACH $400 to PlanHive (include LoanID) — otherwise the offset will reduce rollover-eligible funds.

planbot: Automated: Loan record 990123, balance $400, orig date 2025-08-02. Hardship eligibility: medical expenses qualify; participant must attest that other resources are insufficient.

nina: If PlanHive needs ID verification, can I upload a scanned driver's license or do they require notarized physical copy? I'm in a different time zone this week.

ola: Usually a scanned government ID (front+back) uploaded to the secure portal suffices. If PlanHive requests notarization, they'll explicitly say so — that's rare. During migration, if the portal is flaky, email attachments to support@planhive.com encrypted or via the secure upload link they provide. CC benefits so we can nudge them.

payroll: Also flag: if you become a contractor mid-review, the plan's termination rules still apply. Hardship distribution is processed based on participant's plan status at time of approval. If you switch to 1099 during review, that may change post-approval options (e.g., no rollover of hardship cash-out).

trevor: Tax note: hardship distributions are taxable as ordinary income and may incur 10% early withdrawal penalty if under 59½ unless an exception applies. Hardship distributions are not eligible for direct rollover (plan may allow limited exceptions); check PlanHive decision. If you want to preserve as much as possible, consider whether you can instead take a plan loan or repay outstanding loan via ACH and then request a smaller hardship.

nina: Understood. I'll start the portal case now and email docs. Any sample wording for the cover email to speed things up?

ola: Use concise factual wording, include LoanID and whether you want the loan netted. Example subject: "Hardship Request - nina - LoanID 990123" Body: short bullet list + attach PDFs. Also put preferred phone and timezone. That helps.

planbot: Automated reminder: upload timestamps and case ID will be returned by PlanHive. Keep copies of receipts for tax records.

nina: Thanks all — submitted portal case and emailed docs to support@planhive.com cc benefits@redwood. Subject used as suggested. Will update when I get the case ID. Appreciate the quick replies. :pray:
